Abstract.AbstractText: This study aimed to support training program development through the comparison of performance analysis of professionals mixed martial arts (MMA) athletes in the bouts that were not finished by points. Using digital recordings of each bout, we analyzed 1,564 rounds (678 bouts) which were separated by Ending and other Rounds. Our results indicated that KO/TKO is the main outcome that defines the ending round (≈60%), however, there is a higher frequency of ending by submission on the 1 and 2 round (>30%). Bouts ending during the 1 or 2 rounds had shorter total time and standing combat with low-intensity than ending in the 3 round (91.5±71.4, 93.4±67.5 and 143.2±87.4; for low-intensity in the 1st, 2nd and 3rd round respectively; p<0.05), while standing combat time with high intensity was longer in the last round in comparison to bouts that finished in the 1 or 2 rounds (7.4±9.2, 9.7±18.0 and 17.7±29.1 for high intensity in the 1, 2 and 3 round respectively; p<0.05). The lower time dedicated to low-intensity stand up combat actions, regardless of round, and forcefulness of the actions in groundwork in the 1 and 2 rounds appear to be elements that increase the probability of success in professional MMA bouts, these factors have essential implications related to training program design.
